Parliamentary question | Multilingualism and the role of the French language in the European institutions | E-000921/2023 | European Parliament

# Multilingualism and the role of the French language in the European institutions

20.3.2023

Question for written answer E-000921/2023to the CommissionRule 138Dominique Bilde (ID)

‘Over 90% of European Council and Commission documents, as well as the majority of oral communications of the European institutions, are in the English language’[1].

In the wake of Brexit, ‘English is now the 17thmost common mother tongue among EU citizens’. ‘Less than 2% of residents are native speakers of English’[2].

What is more, ‘there is no common language in the EU spoken at a very good level (native or proficient) by a majority of the population’[3]. And while English is the most commonly taught foreign language in the European Union’s education systems, ‘only 11% of EU residents declare themselves to be proficient in [the language]’[4].

Regulation No 1 determining the languages to be used by the European Economic Community deals with the possibility of determining the languages to be used in the functioning of the institutions (Article 6)[5]. This is addressed in Rule 167 of the Rules of Procedure of the European Parliament[6].

How does the Commission intend to promote multilingualism and the use of French, a language spoken by almost 80% of its officials (2020)[7]?

Submitted: 20.3.2023

- [1] ‘After Brexit, can the primacy of English remain when it is no longer one of the official languages of the EU?’ Louise Mushikiwabo, article published on 6 February 2020, Le Monde.
- [2] ‘Less than 2% of residents are native speakers of English.’ The European Union’s approach to multilingualism in its own communications policy, project leader: Carlos MENDEZ, European Parliament, September 2022.
- [3] ‘There is no common language in the EU spoken at a very good level (native or proficient) by a majority of the population.’
- [4] ‘Only 11% of EU residents declare themselves to be proficient in English’.
- [5] https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A01958R0001-20130701
- [6] https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/RULES-9-2023-01-18-RULE-167_EN.html
- [7] ‘[...] almost 80 percent of Commission officials as of 2020 spoke French.’ https://www.politico.eu/article/in-2022-make-french-language-great-again-eu-presidency/
